clue.text: Protective garment for a mite of sickly appearance

parts.note: someone of sickly appearance looks pale
a mite is a tiny child, a tot

explanation.surface: A coat to protect a poorly-looking little child.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'a mite of sickly appearance' in the order of the pieces' meaning: the colourless (PALE) little one (TOT).
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose overcoat, a garment worn for protection against the weather.

clue.text: Taking a broad view in gold prospecting

definitions.meaning: swinging a camera to film a wide scene
washing gravel in a dish to find gold

explanation.surface: A gold prospector with a wide outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A film camera sweeps horizontally to take in a scene; prospectors swirl gravel in a pan to find nuggets.

clue.text: Improvisations bound to turn out badly

definitions.text: Improvisations bound to turn out badly

parts.words: Improvisations bound to turn out badly
parts.note: makeshift arrangements tied together, so bound in both senses, that are likely to fail

explanation.surface: Makeshift efforts that are doomed to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeshift contraption hastily tied together is informally called this, and such things often fail.

clue.text: Worn out it turns colour

indicators.note: turns means the word it is read the other way round

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something faded, it changes colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted and weary, or worn and stale, are senses of this word.

clue.text: Narrators for whom one may have a sneaking regard

definitions.text: Narrators for whom one may have a sneaking regard

parts.words: Narrators for whom one may have a sneaking regard
parts.note: people who sneak on others, telling stories about them, are regarded as sneaks

explanation.surface: Storytellers one secretly admires.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sneaking regard' is usually a secret fondness; here it means being regarded as a sneak.
explanation.definitionFit: Informers who report others' misdeeds are tattlers, literally tellers of tales.

clue.text: Fit to drink for the likes of Davis and Hendry, say

definitions.text: for the likes of Davis and Hendry, say
definitions.meaning: Steve Davis and Stephen Hendry are snooker champions, so they are able to pot balls

explanation.surface: A drink that suits a pair of snooker champions.
explanation.walkthrough: Davis and Hendry are famous British snooker players; split the answer as POT-ABLE, skilled at potting.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that is drinkable is described with this formal adjective.

clue.text: Asked questions about the model's position

definitions.meaning: put forward a problem or question
an artist's model holds a pose

explanation.surface: Queries about how a model is standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a question is to put it forward; a sitter for an artist holds an attitude.

clue.text: Symptom of canine trouble at times

definitions.text: Symptom of canine trouble at times

parts.words: Symptom of canine trouble at times
parts.note: a canine is a pointed tooth, not a dog, and pain shows it is in trouble

explanation.surface: A sign that a dog is sometimes unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' suggests a dog but means the pointed eye-tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in a tooth is the symptom of dental trouble such as decay.

clue.text: College sphere stocked up with fuel

indicators.note: stocked means filled, so the sphere holds the fuel inside

parts.note: a ball is a sphere

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the fuel is read bottom to top

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A college globe filled with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the fuel from bottom to top; 'stocked' means the sphere is filled with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Balliol is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: New side in an upright position

annotationWithheld.why: New side in an upright position (7): ENDWISE is an anagram of NEW SIDE, but no separate clue word signals the anagram; 'New' would have to be both fodder and indicator.
annotationWithheld.clue: New side in an upright position

clue.text: An opening under the bridge

parts.note: the bridge is the ridge of the nose, and beneath it are the openings for breathing

explanation.surface: A gap beneath a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two breathing openings sits below the bony bridge of the nose.

clue.text: Humoured in a harmful way

parts.note: a child indulged so much it does them harm

explanation.surface: Someone humoured to their own detriment.
explanation.definitionFit: An over-indulged child is damaged by having every whim granted, and the word also means damaged.

clue.text: At home, having no appointment, and overcome

parts.note: being in means being at home
with no date fixed, as an appointment is a date

explanation.surface: Someone at home, with nothing in the diary, is overwhelmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded with work or letters, one is swamped and overwhelmed.

clue.text: A hit of sorts, I conclude, in the Caribbean

indicators.note: the letter I comes to conclude the word, standing at its end
a hit of sorts is a loosely-formed version, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rough sort of success, the speaker decides, somewhere in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of sorts' rearranges A HIT into HAIT, and 'conclude' puts I at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The country occupies the western part of the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: The enthusiasm that got us out

indicators.note: out signals the words are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: The keenness that roused us from bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GOT US.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest and relish for an activity are synonyms of this word.

clue.text: Civic honours make sense in the large corporation

parts.note: OBEs are honours awarded by the British Crown, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: make signals the letters of sense are made into something new

explanation.surface: Civic awards make sense within a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges SENSE into ENESS. 'Corporation' is an old jocular word for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporation is a jocular term for a paunch, so a large one signifies fatness.

clue.text: Bearing of a little beast in heraldry

definitions.text: Bearing of a little beast in heraldry

parts.words: Bearing of a little beast in heraldry
parts.note: a bearing is a charge on a coat of arms, here a small king of beasts

explanation.surface: A heraldic charge depicting a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a small lion shown on a shield is a charge with this diminutive name.

clue.text: One-off dealer on the Stock Exchange?

definitions.text: One-off dealer on the Stock Exchange?

parts.note: a one-off is odd, unlike others
a jobber was a dealer on the London Stock Exchange

explanation.surface: An unusual trader in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1986, jobbers traded shares on the London Stock Exchange; the whole clue playfully describes a casual handyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who does occasional casual jobs is an odd-job worker.

clue.text: Made amends with a change of clothing

explanation.surface: Someone who made up for a wrong by changing their outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy a grievance is to set it right; read as re-dressed it means clothed afresh.

clue.text: Soldiers find it bitter sweet to get going again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
S is short for sweet
tart means sharp-tasting, bitter

explanation.surface: Troops find it a bittersweet experience to resume.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade puts the sweet before the bitter, the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin anew after a pause is to resume or set off once more.

clue.text: Plans a pools permutation that's successful!

parts.note: on the British football pools, punters forecast which matches will be draws
up means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: Someone devising a winning pools entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools were a British betting game in which forecasting score draws won prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft or prepare a document or scheme is to formulate it.

clue.text: Figure said to be insular

indicators.note: said signals that a word spoken aloud gives the answer

parts.note: an ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river, so to be insular is to be like one

explanation.surface: A personality described as narrow-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: An ait is a small river island, as in the Thames; it is pronounced like the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure here is a numeral, and this one comes after seven.

clue.text: Wild llama taking little account of being covered in a fertiliser

indicators.note: the account's short form is covered by the fertiliser around it

parts.note: guano is bird droppings used as fertiliser
AC is the short form of account

explanation.surface: A wild animal paying no attention to being smeared in manure.
explanation.walkthrough: Guano, seabird droppings from South American islands, is a traditional fertiliser, fitting the llama's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: The guanaco is a wild South American camelid, the ancestor of the domesticated llama.

clue.text: A way to take in everybody

definitions.meaning: ... is a London road leading to Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: A road that takes in all and sundry.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MALL is a famous London avenue; split differently the same letters give the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial avenue in London is a route, and read as two other words it means all of a group.

clue.text: Work hard to put aside about a pound

indicators.note: the word for putting aside goes around the pound sign

parts.note: to put money aside is to save it
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Toiling to set aside a pound or so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SAVE around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil like a servant held in bondage is to labour without rest.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink available in bars

explanation.surface: A soft drink you can get in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs but means slabs of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa made with milk is a warm drink, and the same sweet comes moulded in blocks.

clue.text: Part of the body largely used in boxing

definitions.meaning: the upper front of the torso

explanation.surface: A body part that boxers use a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests the sport but means packing things in a large box.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the upper torso, and a big lidded storage box shares the name.

clue.text: Confessed to being a man of property

explanation.surface: Someone admitted to being wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a fact is to acknowledge it; a man of property has possessed things.

clue.text: The south wind bearing east isn't pleasant

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing a quality, standing for the adjective harsh

parts.note: Auster was the Roman god of the south wind

explanation.surface: A southerly turning easterly makes for unpleasant weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster is the classical name for the south wind; 'bearing' simply joins it to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something severe and stern lacks comfort or charm.

clue.text: Also an adorning head-cover in Buenos Aires

indicators.note: in places these words inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: BA is the abbreviation for Buenos Aires
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A decorative scarf worn on the head in Argentina's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adorning' belongs to the definition: the scarf is a decorative head-covering, and 'in' places the joined words inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured kerchief tied over the head is a decorative covering.

clue.text: Born to be a printer?

parts.note: someone whose character is fixed (a ... from birth) also reads as letters arranged for printing

explanation.surface: Someone destined from birth for the printing trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Composing text in movable letters ready for the press is the compositor's job.

clue.text: Bird for which Rufus has a likeness

definitions.text: Bird for which Rufus has a likeness

parts.words: Bird for which Rufus has a likeness
parts.note: Rufus means red-haired, and a poll is a head, so a ginger-headed man resembles this finch

explanation.surface: A bird resembling a red-haired man named Rufus.
explanation.walkthrough: William Rufus, an English king, was so called for his red complexion; poll is an old word for head.
explanation.definitionFit: A small finch with a crimson patch on its crown carries this name.
